about: Does an optimising repairer buy anything, and where does it stop? Two arms in one graph, the same seeded journal, three candidates.

design.informed arm: 150 cycles whose false edge also violates a one-edge law (date order): the choice is available without the two-edge law
design.blind arm: 130 cycles whose false edge violates nothing but the two-edge law: the two edges are indistinguishable, and no information exists to choose between them
design.why: the first arm was the only one measured before, and it is the arm a plain rule can win; the second is the one that can fail

reading: Against a plain rule the gain is real and large: the rule deletes every edge of every violation, so it destroys 150 of 150 true edges on the informed arm; both pgrepair algorithms keep all 150.
Between the ILP and the greedy there is no measurable difference on this workload: 150/150 both on the informed arm, 58/130 and 66/130 on the blind one.

On the blind arm both are at chance, as they must be: 44.6 % and 50.8 %, with a 95 % interval of ±8.6 points on 130 cycles. When two edges carry the same violation and nothing else distinguishes them, no repairer can do better, and the bench says so instead of hiding it.
reserves: 130 blind cycles: the interval is wide, and the design forbids more (only 159 pairs of the whole truth give a blind mirror)
one workload, one truth: this says nothing about constraint sets where violations overlap in richer ways
